title: A ball on the road

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: Do you know the emergency number in your country? Guess: how did Sam help a runner who fell?

chapters.title: A fall near the boulevard
chapters.prompt: CHAPTER 1 SCENE: stone steps near the Baku seaside boulevard, a red-haired bearded man in running clothes kneeling calmly next to an injured runner — a young woman with short blonde hair in a ponytail, no glasses, a bright orange running top — who sits on the steps holding her ankle, a coach in a tracksuit calling on his phone

chapters.title: A close call
chapters.prompt: CHAPTER 2 SCENE: a city street crossing, a little girl reaching for a ball rolling on the road, a car stopping just in time, a woman with round glasses and a lavender sweater rushing to grab her hand

chapters.title: A first aid course
chapters.prompt: CHAPTER 3 SCENE: a bright classroom, a small group of adults practising bandaging each other's arms, a friendly instructor showing how, a first aid kit on the table, NOT the podcast hosts

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is accidents and emergencies. Not the happiest topic, but a useful one.
Very useful. Sam, have you ever called an ambulance?
Once. Last spring, at running club. A woman fell on the stairs near the boulevard and hurt her leg badly.
Oh no. What did you do?
Luckily I did a first aid course last year. I told her not to move, and our coach called the ambulance.
Did you panic?
Inside, a little! But you have to keep a cool head. Everyone was looking at me.
Was it a serious injury?
A broken ankle. But she recovered quickly — she's running again now.
That's good news. I had a close call last month with my niece Aysu.
What happened?
We were crossing the street, and she suddenly ran after her ball. A car stopped just in time.
That must have been terrifying.
My heart stopped. Now she holds my hand on every street, and the ball stays in the bag.
Better safe than sorry.
Exactly. Do you know the emergency number in Azerbaijan?
Is it one-one-two?
Yes, one-one-two. And one-zero-three for an ambulance. Everyone should know them.
Good. I'm saving them in my phone right now. [chuckle]
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: have you ever been in an emergency — and did you keep a cool head?
And maybe it's time for a first aid course! See you next time!
Bye for now!
